**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` function passed to `cors()` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes the request origin back if any of these match:

- `http://localhost:4200`, an exact match (the Angular dev server).
- Any origin ending in `.pages.dev`, at any subdomain depth.
- Any origin ending in `.workers.dev`, at any subdomain depth. This covers the deployed frontend, `https://ai-dnd-frontend.ai-dnd.workers.dev`.

Requests with no `Origin` header, and any other origin, get `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The same middleware also allows methods `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS`, headers `Content-Type` and `Authorization`, and `maxAge: 86400`.

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if (...)` condition inside that `origin` function, at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add one more `||` clause:

- For an exact origin, use `origin === 'https://app.example.com'`.
- For a whole domain, use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`.

Don't add it as an array entry to `origin`. Hono treats array entries as literal strings, so wildcards never match there (see `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4).

An `endsWith` check on a bare suffix such as `.example.com` is safe because of the leading dot. Without the dot, `evilexample.com` would match.

Two follow-ups:

- **Frontend API URL:** if the Worker is also served from a new domain, update the Worker URL in `frontend/src/environments/environment.prod.ts`. This is not needed for CORS.
- **Docs:** `worker/src/index.md` (lines 7 and 25) describes the allowed origins, so update it alongside the code.
